projects.title: ANT Meta Bots – ML-Powered Options Trading Platform
projects.description: An end-to-end algorithmic trading platform that generates ML-based signals and autonomously executes and manages options trades in real time.
highlights: Implemented Lorentzian k-NN ML classification with Rational Quadratic and Gaussian kernel regression for directional signal generation
Automated options execution with dynamic ATM strike selection based on a 5:30 AM IST boundary and HMAC-SHA256 signed API requests
Engineered a cohesive async backend architecture running four concurrent subsystems on strict 1-second cooperative loops
Implemented deterministic trade lifecycle management including crossover-verified entries, TP/SL/trailing stops, re-entry logic, and session-based force-close
Designed a Best-of-N signal scanner and strict direction-slot enforcement to prevent duplicate execution and manage overlapping trade states

architecture: cohesive async Python backend with a React SPA frontend, communicating via REST and native WebSockets
Four concurrent async subsystems (API, BotManager, LiveFeedManager, Watchdog) executing cooperative concurrency on a single event loop
Dual live data feeds separating futures tick streams (for breakout verification) from options tick streams (for TP/SL monitoring)
Layered persistence model combining SQLite for high-frequency signal/trade logs and JSON for bot configuration state
engineering: Translated MQL5 Lorentzian classification algorithm into Python, incorporating RSI/WT/CCI/ADX feature extraction and multi-filter boolean logic
Built Unified Watchdog v4.2 implementing strict Phase 0 (Session), Phase 1 (Scanning), and Phase 2 (Management) execution order
Implemented custom HMAC-SHA256 API client with 3-retry exponential backoff for Delta Exchange communication
Designed WebSocket push-only model broadcasting state and rolling log buffers at 2-3 second intervals
system_design: Adopted singleton pattern for core services (BotInstanceManager, Databases) to avoid dependency injection overhead while maintaining global state
Session-scoped trade isolation mapping trades to a 5:30 AM IST boundary to decouple overlapping day sessions
Separated state mutation (Watchdog) from data ingestion (LiveFeedManager) to prevent race conditions on strict 1-second polling intervals

insights.problem: Maintaining independence between multiple real-time system layers while still enabling meaningful and deterministic interaction between them.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Each subsystem (data manager, live feed, signal generator, trade monitor) had its own independent lifecycle, data format, and execution model, making state synchronization and communication extremely complex to manage without introducing race conditions.
tradeoffs: Cohesive async cooperative concurrency vs. microservices (chosen to minimize inter-process communication latency)
SQLite + JSON persistence vs. PostgreSQL (chosen for zero-setup deployment and sufficient performance for per-bot rolling windows)
Best-of-N signal selection vs. immediate execution (trading slight entry latency for significant noise reduction)
failure_points: API rate limits or network drops during 1-second tick polling (mitigated via 3-retry exponential backoff)
False entries on noisy signal clusters (mitigated via Best-of-N scanner)
Execution-time drift causing wrong expiry selection (mitigated by locking expiry date at exact signal generation time)
insights.real_world_behavior: The system continuously evaluates futures data, identifies optimal breakout entries, and actively trails options prices, force-closing any remaining positions safely at 5:00 PM IST.
insights.what_i_learned: In high-frequency async systems, strict phase-based state machines are essential to prevent race conditions when handling simultaneous data streams.

metrics.scale: Supports concurrent multi-bot execution, each maintaining independent, customizable large-scale memory pools (e.g., 2000+ candles) and dual live tick streams
metrics.latency: 1-second execution cycle for both tick polling (LiveFeedManager) and state evaluation (Watchdog)
metrics.throughput: Continuous async processing of OHLCV history, ML inference, and high-frequency tick streams without thread blocking
metrics.impact: Delivered a fully autonomous, production-ready options trading system with deterministic execution guarantees and zero manual intervention

projects.title: Telegram Signal Distribution System – Event-Driven Trade Execution Pipeline
projects.description: An event-driven Spring Boot application that bridges unstructured Telegram trading signals with MetaTrader 5 execution via a pull-based, concurrent in-memory pipeline.
highlights: Engineered a producer-consumer pipeline utilizing ConcurrentHashMap and ConcurrentLinkedQueue for isolated, per-account signal delivery
Designed a pull-based REST execution system where MT5 clients poll signals every 10 seconds, eliminating push-related delivery failures
Implemented strict multi-regex parsing and price-level validation (e.g., SL < Entry < TP) before queueing unstructured Telegram data
Built a stateful, two-map state machine within the Telegram bot to handle complex multi-step admin CRUD workflows without a web UI
Handled real-time signal lifecycle flows including dynamic market/pending order execution, modification, and cancellation

architecture: Long-polling Telegram consumer bridging unstructured chat signals to a REST-based polling API for MetaTrader 5 clients
In-memory producer-consumer queue system grouping signals by MT5 account ID to ensure isolated, concurrent distribution
Headless backend architecture operated entirely via Telegram bot administrative commands and automated scheduled jobs
JVM Virtual Threads enabled to handle concurrent polling requests efficiently across registered clients
engineering: Enforced TTL-based signal expiry at the queue level: 10 seconds for market orders and 600 seconds for pending orders to prevent stale execution
Developed a custom Exception Hierarchy (ApplicationException) to cleanly route user-facing vs internal errors during API and Bot interactions
Programmed dynamic broker-specific symbol normalization inside the MT5 EA (e.g., appending 'm' for Exness or '.a' for ICM)
Implemented a cron-scheduled JSON backup service that automatically exports the MariaDB users table and sends it to administrators
system_design: Selected a pull-based MT5 architecture to bypass the unreliability and firewall complexities of pushing HTTP requests to client trading terminals
Omitted external message brokers (like RabbitMQ/Kafka) in favor of lightweight concurrent data structures, balancing delivery guarantees with system simplicity
Separated state mutation (Telegram edit/reply events) into distinct signal actions (MODIFIED, CANCEL) parsed gracefully by the MT5 EA

insights.problem: Distributing real-time trading signals from an unreliable, unstructured external source (Telegram) to multiple independent trading accounts without duplication or loss.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Telegram messages are unstructured text, and execution occurs on independent MT5 terminals. This required building strict regex parsing, logical price validation (e.g., verifying SL < Entry < TP), and a synchronization mechanism to prevent stale or duplicate executions.
tradeoffs: Pull-based REST delivery vs. Push-based WebSockets (chosen to bypass MT5 network/firewall constraints)
In-memory ConcurrentLinkedQueues vs. Persistent Message Broker (chosen to minimize infrastructure overhead for ephemeral signals)
Stateful Telegram Bot Admin UI vs. Dedicated Web Frontend (chosen for operational speed and reduced attack surface)
failure_points: Execution of stale signals due to network delays (mitigated by strict 10s TTL for market orders)
Invalid signal formats causing failed trades (prevented by 7-pattern regex matching and pre-queue price sanity checks)
Broker symbol mismatches preventing execution (handled via runtime string normalization in the MT5 EA)
insights.real_world_behavior: The system continuously long-polls Telegram groups, extracts and validates trade data, enqueues it per user, and serves the payloads to MT5 clients polling exactly every 10 seconds.
insights.what_i_learned: In distributed systems integrating with external chat protocols, delivery guarantees, strict payload validation, and client-side pull architectures matter significantly more than raw backend execution speed.

metrics.scale: Supports concurrent isolation and distribution pipelines for multiple registered MT5 accounts
metrics.latency: 10-second polling cycle with near real-time ingestion via Telegram long-polling
metrics.throughput: Processes continuous event streams including new signals, edits, cancellations, and media mirroring
metrics.impact: Eliminated manual trade copying by translating unstructured chat messages into deterministic, multi-account automated executions

projects.title: Quant Discovery Pipeline – Automated Strategy Mining System
projects.description: A high-performance, multi-layer ML pipeline that discovers statistically validated trading strategies by exhaustively simulating trades and learning patterns from enriched market data.
highlights: Engineered a 5-layer (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/Diamond) data pipeline isolating CPU-bound simulation from memory-bound ML normalisation
Utilised Numba JIT to accelerate exhaustive SL/TP trade simulation inner loops to near-C performance across millions of combinations
Implemented dual-terminal outputs: Map-Reduce Decision Tree mining for interpretable rules, and XGBoost binary classification for high-dimensional predictive power
Engineered 300+ features including ATR-normalised distances, TA-Lib candlestick patterns, and multi-anchor relational transforms
Designed chunk-based state management and iterative QuantileDMatrix streaming to process massive datasets on low-RAM environments

architecture: Sequential data pipeline (Bronze → Silver → Gold) that splits into dual terminal paths (Platinum → Diamond) based on desired output
Bronze layer executes exhaustive multi-timeframe trade simulation across customizable SL/TP grids using multiprocessing pools
Silver and Gold layers perform ATR-based swing detection (ZigZag), technical indicator enrichment, and strict rolling Z-score normalisation
Platinum/Diamond layers execute either Map-Reduce blueprint discovery for Decision Trees or Gold⋈Silver inner joins for XGBoost matrix construction
engineering: Integrated TA-Lib C library alongside pandas-native 'ta' library to capture comprehensive candlestick pattern recognition
Replaced native Python loops with Numba JIT compilation in the Bronze layer to process hundreds of millions of (candle, SL, TP) combinations
Implemented explicit buffer flushing to PyArrow Parquet files across all layers to enforce strict peak RAM boundaries
Centralised pipeline configuration (SL/TP ratios, normalisation rules, hyper-parameters) into a single config-driven orchestrator model
system_design: Decoupled computation stages (CPU-bound simulation vs I/O-bound enrichment) into independent modular scripts to allow isolated testing and incremental processing
Supported low-memory environments by implementing iterative XGBoost dataset loading via QuantileDMatrix to bypass full-memory requirements
Enforced a fail-fast execution model where subprocess errors immediately halt the orchestrator to prevent downstream data corruption

insights.problem: Extracting statistically reliable trading edges from massive raw OHLCV datasets where simulation, feature engineering, and ML training each impose conflicting compute and memory constraints.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Evaluating hundreds of millions of trade combinations natively in Python causes severe execution bottlenecks, while merging 300+ features into a single ML dataset easily exceeds standard RAM limits.
tradeoffs: Interpretability (Decision Tree rules) vs. Predictive Power (XGBoost classification)
Full-memory XGBoost training (speed) vs. IterativeDMatrix streaming (low RAM compatibility)
Modular layered architecture (disk I/O overhead) vs. Single monolithic script (memory overflow risk)
failure_points: Out-of-memory (OOM) crashes during the Gold-Silver inner join (mitigated by chunked processing and Parquet sharding)
Data leakage in ML normalisation (prevented by strict temporal train/val splits and rolling Z-score windows)
Python execution bottlenecks in simulation loops (solved via Numba JIT compilation)
insights.real_world_behavior: The orchestrator automatically consumes raw CSV market data, parallel-processes millions of simulations, and outputs either a compiled XGBoost model or explicit, human-readable trading rules without manual intervention.
insights.what_i_learned: At scale, data architecture, chunking strategies, and explicit memory management matter significantly more than the complexity of the underlying ML models.

metrics.scale: Processes hundreds of millions of trade combinations (candle, SL, TP) and 300+ features per execution run
metrics.latency: Reduced simulation execution from hours to minutes by replacing native Python loops with Numba JIT and multiprocessing
metrics.throughput: Continuous, chunked Parquet data flow handling massive datasets across 5 sequential transformation layers
metrics.impact: Provides a fully automated pipeline that transforms raw market data into statistically validated, deployable trading edges

projects.title: Stella – Transactional E-Commerce Backend System
projects.description: A production-style RESTful e-commerce implementing a fully transactional order lifecycle, stateless JWT authentication, and strict 3-tier architectural separation.
highlights: Designed a complete transactional order lifecycle utilizing Razorpay's two-phase payment verification with HMAC-SHA256 signature validation
Implemented stateless JWT authentication enforced via a custom Spring Security filter chain and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Built a distinct 3-tier architecture (Controller, Service, Repository) utilizing Interface Segregation and strict DTO boundaries
Engineered a two-step, database-backed token verification system for user registration and sensitive profile updates via SMTP
Handled multi-part file uploads for product images and store logos using Apache Commons IO with strict extension validation

architecture: 3-tier layered Spring Boot application strictly separating Presentation, Business Logic, and Data Access layers
Stateless backend relying exclusively on a custom JWTAuthenticationFilter and SecurityContextHolder for identity resolution
Local filesystem-based static resource server for media storage, persisting absolute directory paths in the MariaDB database
engineering: Global exception handling implemented via @ControllerAdvice to map internal exceptions to structured HTTP JSON error responses
Two-phase payment workflow managing explicit order states (creating → created → paid) only after cryptographic signature verification
Repository-driven data access leveraging Spring Data JPA's derived queries and CRUD operations, completely abstracting raw SQL
system_design: Enforced strict DTO-to-Entity mapping to prevent over-exposure of the internal database schema to external HTTP clients
Applied the Strategy Pattern across the business layer, requiring all controllers to interact with services via interfaces rather than implementations
Decoupled buyer and seller workflows at the HTTP boundary using Spring Security hasRole() endpoint expressions

insights.problem: Designing a reliable, multi-role e-commerce backend where orders, payments, and user states remain strictly consistent across internal databases and external service integrations.
insights.why_it_was_hard: The system must coordinate internal state transitions with unreliable external systems (Razorpay API, SMTP), requiring robust trust boundaries, cryptographic validation, and multi-step verification flows to prevent state corruption.
tradeoffs: Stateless JWT authentication vs. server-side session management (chosen for RESTful API decoupling)
Monolithic 3-tier simplicity vs. Microservice distribution (chosen for transactional consistency and operational simplicity)
Local filesystem media storage vs. External S3 blob storage (chosen for zero-setup local deployment environments)
failure_points: Payment success callbacks arriving with invalid HMAC-SHA256 signatures (rejected to prevent spoofed order confirmations)
Duplicate payment callbacks attempting to process the same order twice (mitigated by idempotent state checks)
Malicious file upload attempts (mitigated by strict MIME/extension validation before stream execution via Apache Commons IO)
insights.real_world_behavior: Users register, verify identity via SMTP tokens, manage multi-item carts, and initiate orders. The system delegates payment to Razorpay, cryptographically verifies the callback, decrements stock, and triggers fulfillment.
insights.what_i_learned: In distributed transactional systems, the correctness and idempotency of state transitions matter significantly more than feature completeness—especially when integrating external financial APIs.

metrics.scale: Supports independent buyer/seller ecosystems, multi-cart sessions, and up to 9 high-resolution image uploads per product
metrics.latency: Low-latency JSON payload processing utilizing a synchronous Spring Boot HTTP architecture and optimized JPA queries
metrics.throughput: Handles concurrent HTTP requests executing file I/O, relational data mutation, and external API orchestration
metrics.impact: Delivered a structurally sound, production-ready e-commerce API strictly decoupled from client implementations

projects.title: Elastic DCA Engine v4 – Server-Centric Trading State Machine
projects.description: A three-tier, server-authoritative trading engine that transforms MetaTrader 5 into a stateless execution client, enabling deterministic DCA grid strategies, automated hedging, and real-time WebSocket control.
highlights: Built a server-authoritative state machine where MetaTrader 5 acts exclusively as a stateless HTTP polling client
Implemented a pull-based command dispatch queue, preventing MT5 'Context Busy' errors by batching execution commands into single tick responses
Engineered session-scoped trade isolation using UUID-tagged trade comments to automatically detect and clean up orphaned or zombie positions
Developed a merge-on-update concurrency control system that write-protects executed grid rows while allowing live mutation of pending targets
Designed dual independent state-machines for concurrent buy and sell grid execution with dynamic counter-trade hedging logic

architecture: Three-tier event-driven architecture connecting MQL5 EA (Execution), FastAPI Singleton Engine (State), and React UI (Control)
1-second continuous tick loop managing HTTP POST ingestion, state evaluation, action generation, and WebSocket broadcasting
In-memory runtime state (SystemState) paired with SQLite/SQLAlchemy exclusively for persisting named grid configuration presets
Action-queue architecture where the server appends actions internally and flushes them on the EA's next polling request
engineering: Built an asynchronous EA Timeout Watcher background task that forces hard state resets if the MT5 terminal connection drops for more than 10 seconds
Mapped live PnL and trade execution status dynamically by matching MT5 trade comments against active server-side session UUIDs
Implemented instantaneous tick-based crossover detection avoiding look-back dependencies for faster execution triggers
Suppressed high-frequency Uvicorn access logs for 1Hz tick and WebSocket endpoints via custom EndpointFilters to prevent log exhaustion
system_design: Centralized all trading intelligence into the backend singleton, completely decoupling strategy logic from platform-specific MQL5 constraints
Separated state tracking into completely isolated buy and sell state models, supporting asymmetric grid behaviors simultaneously
Adopted an in-memory singleton pattern (DcaEngine) to allow instantaneous state sharing between EA HTTP routers and UI WebSocket routers without thread locking

insights.problem: Maintaining strict, reliable execution state across an external execution terminal (MetaTrader) and an authoritative backend engine.
insights.why_it_was_hard: The MT5 terminal and backend operate asynchronously. Network delays, missed ticks, or terminal restarts easily cause state desynchronization, incorrect PnL mapping, and severe trade duplication risks.
tradeoffs: Pull-based action queue (avoids MT5 thread locking) vs. Server-push via WebSockets (lower latency but harder MT5 network integration)
In-memory singleton state (zero-latency evaluation) vs. Database-backed runtime state (crash recovery persistence)
Strict immutable executed rows vs. Allowing full manual override during live sessions
failure_points: Zombie/orphan trades persisting from previous sessions (mitigated by strict UUID session-ID tagging on trade comments)
MT5 'Context Busy' execution errors during rapid market moves (solved via batched array responses on the 1-second tick poll)
Network drops leaving the backend unaware of terminal state (handled by 10-second EA timeout background watcher)
UI overriding live executed rows (prevented by the merge-on-update validation logic)
insights.real_world_behavior: The Python engine continually evaluates ingested tick data, generates precise action commands, and serves them to the polling MT5 client, while simultaneously streaming live state to the React dashboard via WebSockets.
insights.what_i_learned: Reliable distributed execution requires strict shared contracts and deterministic state transitions, rather than assuming external platforms will perfectly execute commands.

metrics.scale: Simultaneously processes multiple independent DCA grids (buy/sell) with multi-row tracking, TP/SL, and dynamic hedging targets
metrics.latency: Tick-driven 1-second continuous evaluation and response cycle across EA, backend, and UI layers
metrics.throughput: Constant 1Hz state evaluation, payload serialization, and WebSocket broadcasting loop
metrics.impact: Successfully isolated algorithmic trading logic from MT5 terminal limitations, resulting in a deterministic, robust execution pipeline

projects.title: Rubik's Cube Solver — State-Space Search & Optimization Engine
projects.description: A terminal-based C++17 Rubik's Cube solving engine that applies the CFOP method and multi-start local search to compute near-optimal solutions without external dependencies.
highlights: Built a state-space search engine in pure C++17 evaluating thousands of candidate CFOP solutions per execution
Implemented multi-start local search across all 6 cube orientations to approximate globally optimal move counts
Designed a custom macro-based DSL and side-rotation remapping engine to execute universal algorithms across any cube face
Engineered an iterative move-cancellation optimizer and stochastic F2L step randomization via std::mt19937 for solution diversity
Modeled the 3D cube state using multidimensional vectors with value semantics, bypassing complex undo-stacks via prototype copy-constructors

architecture: Single-process CLI application executing a modular CFOP (Cross → F2L → OLL → PLL) pipeline
Core state maintained in a 3-dimensional vector representation (CubeMain[6][3][3]) acting as a single source of truth
Orchestrator layer (CubeSolver) instantiates and drives independent solver stages using Template Method overriding
engineering: Developed entirely without third-party dependencies using standard C++17 STL and pure ANSI escape codes for step-by-step terminal rendering
Created a setalgo function to parse string-based move tokens and dynamically remap slice rotations relative to non-default target faces
Implemented deterministic pattern matching for OLL/PLL stages using long integer and string state fingerprints
system_design: Used prototype copy-constructors to cheaply clone cube states at intermediate solver boundaries, avoiding complex undo/rollback state logic
Separated state mutation primitives (in-place matrix updates) from solution-tracking vectors to allow safe algorithmic branch exploration
Designed deterministic (OLL/PLL) and stochastic (F2L) solving phases combined with up to 4 multi-pass reduction rules for final move compression

insights.problem: Efficiently solving a combinatorial puzzle with a massive state space (~43 quintillion states) using strictly bounded memory and execution time.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Balancing solution optimality against raw computation time required modeling complex 3D rotations accurately and evaluating thousands of branching paths without introducing memory leaks or relying on heavy pointer tracking.
tradeoffs: Exhaustive multi-start local search vs. heuristic node pruning (chosen to ensure optimal Cross/F2L sequence selection)
Value semantics via copying full cube state vs. maintaining a sequential undo stack (chosen for architectural simplicity and stage isolation)
Terminal ANSI rendering vs. external GUI libraries (chosen to maintain a strict zero-dependency build)
failure_points: Initial brute-force search approaches exhausted memory and compute time before reaching valid solutions
Side-rotation remapping logic initially caused incorrect state mutations when executing standard algorithms on non-front faces
Redundant consecutive moves (e.g., U followed by U') bloated the final output (solved via static multi-pass Optimiser)
insights.real_world_behavior: The application interactively validates 54 color inputs, generates thousands of candidate paths across 6 orientations, and sequentially plays back the shortest sequence (<42 moves) using colored terminal animation.
insights.what_i_learned: When dealing with massive state spaces, constraining the search area with domain-specific heuristics (CFOP) and utilizing cheap state copying is often far more efficient and manageable than pure brute-force calculation.

metrics.scale: Evaluates 6xN solution trees across all cube orientations utilizing randomized F2L branching
metrics.latency: Consistently computes and optimizes near-optimal solutions in approximately 2 seconds
metrics.throughput: Evaluates state transitions sequentially in memory, processing thousands of generated nodes per execution cycle
metrics.impact: Delivered a highly optimized, cross-platform algorithmic solver built entirely on standard library primitives

projects.title: Lorentzian ML Engine – Cross-Platform Signal Generation System
projects.description: A cross-language, deterministic implementation of a Lorentzian-distance KNN trading strategy, engineered from Pine Script to strict parity in MQL5 and Python without external ML libraries.
highlights: Achieved 100% deterministic cross-language parity by reverse-engineering native Pine Script indicators and execution semantics into independent MQL5 and Python libraries
Implemented a non-parametric K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm utilizing a non-linear Lorentzian distance metric tailored for volatile financial time-series data
Designed a zero-dependency Python ML engine employing a fully customizable, fixed-size historical ring buffer supporting dynamic training, backtesting, and inference windows
Engineered dual Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression estimators (Rational Quadratic and Gaussian) serving as strict trend-confirmation gates for the primary KNN predictions
Constructed a multi-gate boolean filter pipeline combining custom ATR volatility tracking, Kalman-like regime filters, and ADX thresholds to suppress low-probability signals

architecture: Three parallel, decoupled implementations sharing identical data structures, naming conventions, and mathematical logic across Pine Script, MQL5, and Python
Three-phase pipeline architecture (Warmup → Training → Backtest/Live) operating on a configurable historical window instead of a fixed 2750-bar constraint
Per-bar state embedding design where every S_BarData record carries its full intermediate indicator state, enabling O(1) step-forward calculations without global accumulators
engineering: Replaced Euclidean distance with a custom logarithmic Lorentzian distance metric to naturally discount black-swan outliers in historical price comparisons
Optimized the O(N) KNN search algorithm to O(0.75·N) by implementing a modulo-4 filtering rule to skip redundant adjacent training candidates
Warped the KNN neighbor selection threshold to the 75th percentile of the active candidate pool, continuously refining the cluster density toward high-conviction historical matches
Assigned target training labels (y_label) strictly 4 bars in arrears to guarantee zero look-ahead bias during the live prediction phase
system_design: Decoupled signal generation logic entirely from execution environments, allowing the Python module to act as a stateless, pure-function library for external trading bots
Bypassed heavy dependencies like pandas or scikit-learn by rebuilding core normalization, exponential moving averages (RMA/EMA), and regression functions in standard Python
Utilized explicit dataclasses for strict, type-safe configuration injection (StrategySettings, FilterSettings, KernelSettings) avoiding hidden environment variables

insights.problem: Replicating a complex, TradingView-exclusive Pine Script ML algorithm with 100% data flow parity in restrictive, non-browser languages (MQL5 and Python).
insights.why_it_was_hard: Converting Pine Script is not a syntax translation; it requires reverse-engineering TradingView's implicit execution model, native indicator states, and historical data handling into an explicitly managed data structure that respects MQL5 constraints while remaining optimal in Python.
tradeoffs: Zero external dependencies (requires complex custom math logic) vs. Importing heavy libraries like scikit-learn (slower execution, breaks cross-language structural parity)
Fixed-size ring buffers with configurable windows (strict memory control) vs. dynamically growing lists (simpler but unsafe for long-running systems)
Lorentzian distance metric (computationally heavier log calculations) vs. Euclidean distance (faster but highly sensitive to price anomalies)
failure_points: Accumulated floating-point drift in RMA/EMA calculations causing delayed signal divergence between MT5 and Python (solved by mirroring exact per-bar state objects)
Look-ahead bias corrupting the ML training labels during backtesting (solved by strict 4-bar delayed assignment)
O(N) performance degradation during high-frequency live polling (mitigated via the modulo-4 KNN skip optimization)
insights.real_world_behavior: The engine consumes raw OHLCV streams, initializes configurable historical data windows in milliseconds, and deterministically computes live directional probabilities, gating them through volatility and kernel filters before emitting trade signals.
insights.what_i_learned: Porting complex financial algorithms across languages requires mapping the hidden execution context and state-management lifecycle of the origin platform, not just translating the mathematical syntax.

metrics.scale: Supports fully customizable historical windows, typically structured as ~2000 training bars, ~500 pre-launch backtest bars, and ~250 indicator warmup bars (adjustable based on strategy requirements)
metrics.latency: Real-time O(maxBarsBack) inference execution completing in sub-millisecond durations per new candle close
metrics.throughput: Continuous, tickless signal generation optimized specifically for closed-candle step processing without global state locks
metrics.impact: Successfully liberated a proprietary TradingView strategy into a robust, deployable programmatic core that actively powers production trading systems.

projects.title: ELISA
projects.description: A self-hosted, multi-service voice assistant that replicates the full conversational AI pipeline (speech → intent → execution) using a local-first architecture without relying on large language models.
highlights: Architected a multi-service pipeline isolating physical audio I/O, natural language understanding, and business logic over HTTP REST boundaries.
Implemented an end-to-end offline speech pipeline (wake word → VAD → STT → NLU → TTS) achieving full voice interaction without external APIs.
Implemented a local-first speech pipeline using OpenWakeWord, WebRTC VAD, and Whisper.cpp with zero cloud API dependencies.
Designed a hybrid NLU pipeline combining probabilistic intent classification (DIET) with deterministic temporal entity extraction (Duckling).
Built a persistent background scheduling system with APScheduler and SQLite, supporting dual-trigger alerts and fuzzy-matched CRUD operations.
Engineered dynamic hardware management, implementing explicit PyAudio instance release protocols to prevent single-microphone contention.
Designed a production-style conversational pipeline mimicking modern AI assistants, decomposing speech understanding into deterministic and probabilistic subsystems.

architecture: System designed to emulate real-world AI assistant architectures where each layer operates as an independently deployable service.
Multi-service layered topology consisting of Assistant (Runtime Orchestrator), NLU (Rasa + Duckling), and Logic (FastAPI) layers.
Unidirectional data flow enforcing strict downward propagation: Assistant -> NLU -> Logic, preventing lateral state entanglement.
Containerized infrastructure for Coqui TTS and Duckling communicating with the host-native Python orchestration via Docker Compose and bridge networks.
Dual-featurization pipeline utilizing spaCy 300-dimensional word embeddings and CountVectors for robust semantic and morphological analysis.
engineering: Integrated WebRTC VAD with aggressiveness level 2 and a ring buffer requiring 80% voiced frames for onset and 90% unvoiced for offset detection.
Implemented cross-platform app launching by parsing Linux .desktop files and Windows .lnk shortcuts with difflib-based fuzzy matching (0.6 cutoff).
Configured fallback threshold at 0.3 with 0.1 ambiguity margins to gracefully degrade to deterministic error states instead of misclassifying intents.
Exposed real-time system state (boot, listening, processing) to a Web UI via an async WebSocket server utilizing thread-safe message queues.
system_design: Isolated each layer into its own process and Python virtual environment to guarantee zero shared imports and enable independent scaling or component replacement.
Positioned Duckling temporally late in the NLU pipeline to guarantee deterministic ISO 8601 parsing overrides any conflicting DIET probabilistic extractions.
Designed the wake word listener to enforce a 3-second cooldown, preventing self-activation loops triggered by residual TTS audio output.
Implemented a TEDPolicy and MemoizationPolicy for multi-turn conversations alongside strict deterministic rules for direct logic integrations.

insights.problem: Understanding how modern conversational AI systems process raw human speech into structured, executable actions across multiple independent layers without relying on large language models.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Managing continuous microphone polling concurrently with speech-to-text recording, alongside coordinating multi-turn contextual state across strictly isolated HTTP services.
tradeoffs: Chose the DIET classifier over pre-trained transformers to eliminate GPU hardware requirements, prioritizing local-execution compatibility over raw model scale.
Accepted slight HTTP serialization overhead between layers in exchange for absolute process isolation and testability.
Utilized Duckling for dates/times instead of purely ML-based extraction to guarantee the exact structural precision needed for the APScheduler subsystem.
failure_points: Single-microphone contention between OpenWakeWord and VAD recording; resolved by forcefully terminating PyAudio streams and yielding the device before invoking callbacks.
Transient speech recognition failures; mitigated by a 3-attempt state-machine retry loop.
Subsystem outages; handled via isolation so that if the Logic API fails, NLU gracefully returns error text while preserving conversational intents like greetings.
Ambiguous user reminder deletions; handled by implementing a 0.5 cutoff fuzzy matching algorithm against active SQLite job stores.
insights.real_world_behavior: Runs continuously as a background multi-process system, handling asynchronous background jobs while executing synchronous voice pipelines that gracefully degrade upon partial component failure.
insights.what_i_learned: Modern AI systems are not just larger models but tightly integrated pipelines; building ELISA clarified how LLMs abstract away orchestration complexity by embedding reasoning, memory, and intent understanding into a single unified model.

metrics.scale: 3 distinct service layers, 2 containerized instances, 20 NLU intents, 500-epoch DIET training model
metrics.latency: ~200ms generation latency for short neural TTS utterances; 3-second enforced wake word cooldown
metrics.throughput: Processes 1 active conversation pipeline synchronously while managing concurrent background task schedulers
metrics.impact: 100% local, telemetry-free voice control system capable of persistent scheduling and desktop application execution

projects.title: Classical NLP Command Engine
projects.description: A deterministic NLP engine that reconstructs structured command understanding from first principles using dependency parsing, NER, and rule-based semantic mapping — without relying on LLMs.
highlights: Built a deterministic NLP pipeline that extracts action, agent, semantic roles, and normalized timestamps from raw text using classical NLP primitives.
Designed an NER-first entity resolution pipeline prioritizing multi-word entity recognition over POS-based fallbacks.
Built a semantic role mapping engine using dependency relations and preposition-aware heuristics.
Developed a dual-tier temporal normalization strategy combining Facebook's Duckling sidecar with a custom Dateparser fallback engine.
Separated modifiers from embedded parameters via syntactic rule checks on dependency relations (e.g., amod vs. nmod/obl).

architecture: Multi-stage text processing pipeline wrapping a Stanza statistical model core with a custom deterministic rule engine.
Two-mode execution architecture: a FastAPI HTTP server for RESTful service operations and an interactive REPL shell for debugging.
Centralized deterministic parsing core to maintain full pipeline traceability and simplify debugging of linguistic transformations.
Sidecar containerization pattern deploying Duckling on an isolated port for external temporal entity resolution.
engineering: Extracted metadata, task structures, and pragmatics strictly traversing Stanza's dependency tree as the single source of truth.
Merged fragmented time references (e.g., 'tomorrow' + 'morning') into unified strings prior to normalization to improve temporal accuracy.
Cached Stanza statistical models at system startup to prevent per-request loading latency.
Implemented syntactic separation to classify children nodes as modifiers (amod, nummod) or distinct semantic entities (nmod, obl).
system_design: Relied entirely on explicit dependency mapping rather than Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) ML models to maintain absolute predictability and inspectability.
Designed an explicit fallback chain for entity resolution: Named Entity Recognition -> POS tags -> custom mapping rules.
Structured the application with a thin API wrapper over a purely logic-driven core to ensure testing capabilities independent of network state.

insights.problem: Investigating the limits of classical, rule-based NLP primitives in extracting structured, machine-readable JSON commands without relying on the generalized inference of LLMs.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Time expression fragmentation and the inherent cascading failure risk where a single incorrect dependency parse ruins the entire downstream semantic role assignment.
tradeoffs: Prioritized absolute predictability and inspectability of rule-based assignments over the higher tolerance for ambiguity inherent to transformer models.
Chose to build a monolithic core logic file to explicitly document the complete deterministic pipeline flow at the expense of strict module separation.
Relied on Stanza's statistical NER models first before falling back to manual POS heuristics, blending statistical probability with deterministic rules.
failure_points: Inevitably fails at resolving linguistic ambiguity, implicit meaning, and multi-turn contextual tracking.
Ungrammatical sentences produce incorrect dependency trees, causing unrecoverable cascading extraction errors.
Duckling unavailability forces a fallback to the less robust Dateparser engine, degrading complex temporal normalization.
insights.real_world_behavior: Performs deterministically and predictably for well-formed, single-sentence commands, but degrades sharply when exposed to ambiguous or conversational language.
insights.what_i_learned: Rule-based pipeline NLP cannot match modern LLM capability in handling edge cases and implicit meaning, demonstrating clear boundaries between deterministic linguistic extraction and learned generalization. This highlighted why modern systems collapse multiple NLP stages into unified neural architectures instead of modular pipelines.
